Wear shoes an ell in height,—the truth betrays thee,
And thou remainest—what thou art.

gabinete_2_0370.speaker: faust
stanzas: I feel, indeed, that I have made the treasure
Of human thought and knowledge mine, in vain;
And if I now sit down in restful leisure,
No fount of newer strength is in my brain:
I am no hair’s-breadth more in height,
Nor nearer, to the Infinite,

gabinete_2_0376.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Good Sir, you see the facts precisely
As they are seen by each and all.
We must arrange them now, more wisely,
Before the joys of life shall pall.
Why, Zounds! Both hands and feet are, truly—
And head and virile forces—thine:
Yet all that I indulge in newly,
Is’t thence less wholly mine?
If I’ve six stallions in my stall,
Are not their forces also lent me?
I speed along, completest man of all,
As though my legs were four-and-twenty.
Take hold, then! let reflection rest,
And plunge into the world with zest!
I say to thee, a speculative wight
Is like a beast on moorlands lean,
That round and round some fiend misleads to evil plight,
While all about lie pastures fresh and green.

gabinete_2_0396.speaker: faust
stanzas: Then how shall we begin?

gabinete_2_0397.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: We’ll try a wider sphere.
What place of martyrdom is here!
Is’t life, I ask, is’t even prudence,
To bore thyself and bore the students?
Let Neighbor Paunch to that attend!
Why plague thyself with threshing straw forever?
The best thou learnest, in the end
Thou dar’st not tell the youngsters—never!
I hear one’s footsteps, hither steering.

gabinete_2_0410.speaker: faust
stanzas: To see him now I have no heart.

gabinete_2_0412.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: So long the poor boy waits a hearing,
He must not unconsoled depart.
Thy cap and mantle straightway lend me!
I’ll play the comedy with art.

gabinete_2_0416.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He disguises himself.

gabinete_2_0417.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: My wits, be certain, will befriend me.
But fifteen minutes’ time is all I need;
For our fine trip, meanwhile, prepare thyself with speed!

gabinete_2_0422.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Exit FAUST.

gabinete_2_0422.speaker: narrator
stanzas: In FAUST’S long mantle.

gabinete_2_0423.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Reason and Knowledge only thou despise,
The highest strength in man that lies!
Let but the Lying Spirit bind thee
With magic works and shows that blind thee,
And I shall have thee fast and sure!—
Fate such a bold, untrammelled spirit gave him,
As forwards, onwards, ever must endure;
Whose over-hasty impulse drave him
Past earthly joys he might secure.
Dragged through the wildest life, will I enslave him,
Through flat and stale indifference;
With struggling, chilling, checking, so deprave him
That, to his hot, insatiate sense,
The dream of drink shall mock, but never lave him:
Refreshment shall his lips in vain implore—
Had he not made himself the Devil’s, naught could save
him,
Still were he lost forevermore!

gabinete_2_0447.speaker: narrator
stanzas: A STUDENT enters.

gabinete_2_0448.speaker: student
stanzas: A short time, only, am I here,
And come, devoted and sincere,
To greet and know the man of fame,
Whom men to me with reverence name.

gabinete_2_0452.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Your courtesy doth flatter me:
You see a man, as others be.
Have you, perchance, elsewhere begun?

gabinete_2_0455.speaker: student
stanzas: Receive me now, I pray, as one
Who comes to you with courage good,
Somewhat of cash, and healthy blood:
My mother was hardly willing to let me;
But knowledge worth having I fain would get me.

gabinete_2_0463.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Then you have reached the right place now.

gabinete_2_0465.speaker: student
stanzas: I’d like to leave it, I must avow;
I find these walls, these vaulted spaces
Are anything but pleasant places.
Tis all so cramped and close and mean;
One sees no tree, no glimpse of green,
And when the lecture-halls receive me,
Seeing, hearing, and thinking leave me.

gabinete_2_0473.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: All that depends on habitude.
So from its mother’s breasts a child
At first, reluctant, takes its food,
But soon to seek them is beguiled.
Thus, at the breasts of Wisdom clinging,
Thou’lt find each day a greater rapture bringing.

gabinete_2_0481.speaker: student
stanzas: I’ll hang thereon with joy, and freely drain them;
But tell me, pray, the proper means to gain them.

gabinete_2_0483.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Explain, before you further speak,
The special faculty you seek.

gabinete_2_0486.speaker: student
stanzas: I crave the highest erudition;
And fain would make my acquisition
All that there is in Earth and Heaven,
In Nature and in Science too.

gabinete_2_0490.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Here is the genuine path for you;
Yet strict attention must be given.

gabinete_2_0493.speaker: student
stanzas: Body and soul thereon I’ll wreak;
Yet, truly, I’ve some inclination
On summer holidays to seek
A little freedom and recreation.

gabinete_2_0498.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Use well your time! It flies so swiftly from us;
But time through order may be won, I promise.
So, Friend (my views to briefly sum),
First, the collegium logicum.
There will your mind be drilled and braced,
As if in Spanish boots ’twere laced,
And thus, to graver paces brought,
’Twill plod along the path of thought,
Instead of shooting here and there,
A will-o’-the-wisp in murky air.
Days will be spent to bid you know,
What once you did at a single blow,
Like eating and drinking, free and strong,—
That one, two, three! thereto belong.
Truly the fabric of mental fleece
Resembles a weaver’s masterpiece,
Where a thousand threads one treadle throws,
Where fly the shuttles hither and thither.
Unseen the threads are knit together.
And an infinite combination grows.
Then, the philosopher steps in
And shows, no otherwise it could have been:
The first was so, the second so,
Therefore the third and fourth are so;
Were not the first and second, then
The third and fourth had never been.
The scholars are everywhere believers,
But never succeed in being weavers.
He who would study organic existence,
First drives out the soul with rigid persistence;
Then the parts in his hand he may hold and class,
But the spiritual link is lost, alas!
Encheiresin natures, this Chemistry names,
Nor knows how herself she banters and blames!

gabinete_2_0558.speaker: student
stanzas: I cannot understand you quite.

gabinete_2_0559.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Your mind will shortly be set aright,
When you have learned, all things reducing,
To classify them for your using.

gabinete_2_0563.speaker: student
stanzas: I feel as stupid, from all you’ve said,
As if a mill-wheel whirled in my head!

gabinete_2_0566.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: And after—first and foremost duty—Of
Metaphysics learn the use and beauty!
See that you most profoundly gain
What does not suit the human brain!
A splendid word to serve, you’ll find
For what goes in—or won’t go in—your mind.
But first, at least this half a year,
To order rigidly adhere;
Five hours a day, you understand,
And when the clock strikes, be on hand!
Prepare beforehand for your part
With paragraphs all got by heart,
So you can better watch, and look
That naught is said but what is in the book:
Yet in thy writing as unwearied be,
As did the Holy Ghost dictate to thee!

gabinete_2_0590.speaker: student
stanzas: No need to tell me twice to do it!
I think, how useful ’tis to write;
For what one has, in black and white,
One carries home and then goes through it.

gabinete_2_0594.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Yet choose thyself a faculty!

gabinete_2_0596.speaker: student
stanzas: I cannot reconcile myself to Jurisprudence.

gabinete_2_0598.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Nor can I therefore greatly blame you students:
I know what science this has come to be.
All rights and laws are still transmitted
Like an eternal sickness of the race,—
From generation unto generation fitted,
And shifted round from place to place.
Reason becomes a sham, Beneficence a worry:
Thou art a grandchild, therefore woe to thee!
The right born with us, ours in verity,
This to consider, there’s, alas! no hurry.

gabinete_2_0611.speaker: student
stanzas: My own disgust is strengthened by your speech:
O lucky he, whom you shall teach!
I’ve almost for Theology decided.

gabinete_2_0615.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: I should not wish to see you here misguided:
For, as regards this science, let me hint
’Tis very hard to shun the false direction;
There’s so much secret poison lurking in ’t,
So like the medicine, it baffles your detection.
Hear, therefore, one alone, for that is best, in sooth,
And simply take your master’s words for truth.
On words let your attention centre!
Then through the safest gate you’ll enter
The temple-halls of Certainty.

gabinete_2_0631.speaker: student
stanzas: Yet in the word must some idea be.

gabinete_2_0634.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Of course! But only shun too over-sharp a tension,
For just where fails the comprehension,
A word steps promptly in as deputy.
With words ’tis excellent disputing;
Systems to words ’tis easy suiting;
On words ’tis excellent believing;
No word can ever lose a jot from thieving.

gabinete_2_0648.speaker: student
stanzas: Pardon! With many questions I detain you.
Yet must I trouble you again.
Of Medicine I still would fain
Hear one strong word that might explain you.
Three years is but a little space.
And, God! who can the field embrace?
If one some index could be shown,
’Twere easier groping forward, truly.

gabinete_2_0656.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: I’m tired enough of this dry tone,—
Must play the Devil again, and fully.

gabinete_2_0660.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Aloud

gabinete_2_0661.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: To grasp the spirit of Medicine is easy:
Learn of the great and little world your fill,
To let it go at last, so please ye,
Just as God will!
In vain that through the realms of science you may drift;
Each one learns only—just what learn he can:
Yet he who grasps the Moment’s gift,
He is the proper man.
Well-made you are, ’tis not to be denied,
The rest a bold address will win you;
If you but in yourself confide,
At once confide all others in you.
To lead the women, learn the special feeling!
Their everlasting aches and groans,
In thousand tones,
Have all one source, one mode of healing;
And if your acts are half discreet,
You’ll always have them at your feet.
A title first must draw and interest them,
And show that yours all other arts exceeds;
Then, as a greeting, you are free to touch and test them,
While, thus to do, for years another pleads.
You press and count the pulse’s dances,
And then, with burning sidelong glances,
You clasp the swelling hips, to see
If tightly laced her corsets be.

gabinete_2_0705.speaker: student
stanzas: That’s better, now! The How and Where, one sees.

gabinete_2_0709.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: My worthy friend, gray are all theories,
And green alone Life’s golden tree.

gabinete_2_0713.speaker: student
stanzas: I swear to you, ’tis like a dream to me.
Might I again presume, with trust unbounded,
To hear your wisdom thoroughly expounded?

gabinete_2_0717.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Most willingly, to what extent I may.

gabinete_2_0718.speaker: student
stanzas: I cannot really go away:
Allow me that my album first I reach you,—
Grant me this favor, I beseech you!

gabinete_2_0718.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Assuredly.

gabinete_2_0722.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He writes, and returns the book.

gabinete_2_0723.speaker: student
stanzas: Eritis sicut Deus, scientes bonum et malum.

gabinete_2_0724.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Closes the book with reverence, and withdraws

gabinete_2_0725.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Follow the ancient text, and the snake thou wast ordered to trample!
With all thy likeness to God, thou’lt yet be a sorry example!

gabinete_2_0729.speaker: narrator
stanzas: FAUST enters.

gabinete_2_0730.speaker: faust
stanzas: Now, whither shall we go?

gabinete_2_0731.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: As best it pleases thee.
The little world, and then the great, we’ll see.
With what delight, what profit winning,
Shalt thou sponge through the term beginning!

gabinete_2_0738.speaker: faust
stanzas: Yet with the flowing beard I wear,
Both ease and grace will fail me there.
The attempt, indeed, were a futile strife;
I never could learn the ways of life.
I feel so small before others, and thence
Should always find embarrassments.

gabinete_2_0744.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: My friend, thou soon shalt lose all such misgiving:
Be thou but self-possessed, thou hast the art of living!

gabinete_2_0746.speaker: faust
stanzas: How shall we leave the house, and start?
Where hast thou servant, coach and horses?

gabinete_2_0749.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: We’ll spread this cloak with proper art,
Then through the air direct our courses.
But only, on so bold a flight,
Be sure to have thy luggage light.
A little burning air, which I shall soon prepare us,
Above the earth will nimbly bear us,
And, if we’re light, we’ll travel swift and clear:
I gratulate thee on thy new career!

taberna_auerbach_0002.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Is no one laughing? no one drinking?
I’ll teach you how to grin, I’m thinking.
To-day you’re like wet straw, so tame;
And usually you’re all aflame.

taberna_auerbach_0006.speaker: brander
stanzas: Now that’s your fault; from you we nothing see,
No beastliness and no stupidity.

taberna_auerbach_0006.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Pours a glass of wine over BRANDER’S head.

taberna_auerbach_0009.speaker: frosch
stanzas: There’s both together!

taberna_auerbach_0011.speaker: brander
stanzas: Twice a swine!

taberna_auerbach_0012.speaker: frosch
stanzas: You wanted them: I’ve given you mine.

taberna_auerbach_0013.speaker: siebel
stanzas: Turn out who quarrels—out the door!
With open throat sing chorus, drink and roar!
Up! holla! ho!

taberna_auerbach_0017.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Woe’s me, the fearful bellow!
Bring cotton, quick! He’s split my ears, that fellow.

taberna_auerbach_0019.speaker: siebel
stanzas: When the vault echoes to the song,
One first perceives the bass is deep and strong.

taberna_auerbach_0021.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Well said! and out with him that takes the least offence!
Ah, tara, lara da!

taberna_auerbach_0021.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Ah, tara, lara, da!

taberna_auerbach_0021.speaker: frosch
stanzas: The throats are tuned, commence!

taberna_auerbach_0023.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Sings.

taberna_auerbach_0024.speaker: frosch
stanzas: The dear old holy Roman realm,
How does it hold together?

taberna_auerbach_0026.speaker: brander
stanzas: A nasty song! Fie! a political song—
A most offensive song! Thank God, each morning, therefore,
That you have not the Roman realm to care for!
At least, I hold it so much gain for me,
That I nor Chancellor nor Kaiser be.
Yet also we must have a ruling head, I hope,
And so we’ll choose ourselves a Pope.
You know the quality that can
Decide the choice, and elevate the man.

taberna_auerbach_0046.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Soar up, soar up, Dame Nightingale!
Ten thousand times my sweetheart hail!

taberna_auerbach_0050.speaker: siebel
stanzas: No, greet my sweetheart not! I tell you, I’ll resent it.

taberna_auerbach_0052.speaker: frosch
stanzas: My sweetheart greet and kiss! I dare you to prevent it!

taberna_auerbach_0054.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Sings.

taberna_auerbach_0055.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Draw the latch! the darkness makes:
Draw the latch! the lover wakes.
Shut the latch! the morning breaks.

taberna_auerbach_0063.speaker: siebel
stanzas: Yes, sing away, sing on, and praise, and brag of her!
I’ll wait my proper time for laughter:
Me by the nose she led, and now she’ll lead you after.
Her paramour should be an ugly gnome,
Where four roads cross, in wanton play to meet her:
An old he-goat, from Blocksberg coming home,
Should his good-night in lustful gallop bleat her!
A fellow made of genuine flesh and blood
Is for the wench a deal too good.
Greet her? Not I: unless, when meeting,
To smash her windows be a greeting!

taberna_auerbach_0084.speaker: brander
stanzas: Attention! Hearken now to me!
Confess, Sirs, I know how to live.
Enamored persons here have we,
And I, as suits their quality,
Must something fresh for their advantage give.
Take heed! ’Tis of the latest cut, my strain,
And all strike in at each refrain!

taberna_auerbach_0096.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He sings.

taberna_auerbach_0097.speaker: brander
stanzas: There was a rat in the cellar-nest,
Whom fat and butter made smoother:
He had a paunch beneath his vest
Like that of Doctor Luther.
The cook laid poison cunningly,
And then as sore oppressed was he
As if he had love in his bosom.

taberna_auerbach_0109.speaker: chorus
stanzas: As if he had love in his bosom!

taberna_auerbach_0111.speaker: brander
stanzas: He ran around, he ran about,
His thirst in puddles laving;
He gnawed and scratched the house throughout.
But nothing cured his raving.
He whirled and jumped, with torment mad,
And soon enough the poor beast had,
As if he had love in his bosom.

taberna_auerbach_0123.speaker: chorus
stanzas: As if he had love in his bosom!

taberna_auerbach_0125.speaker: brander
stanzas: And driven at last, in open day,
He ran into the kitchen,
Fell on the hearth, and squirming lay,
In the last convulsion twitching.
Then laughed the murderess in her glee:
“Ha! ha! he’s at his last gasp,” said she,
“As if he had love in his bosom!”

taberna_auerbach_0137.speaker: chorus
stanzas: As if he had love in his bosom!

taberna_auerbach_0139.speaker: siebel
stanzas: How the dull fools enjoy the matter!
To me it is a proper art
Poison for such poor rats to scatter.

taberna_auerbach_0143.speaker: brander
stanzas: Perhaps you’ll warmly take their part?

taberna_auerbach_0143.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: The bald-pate pot-belly I have noted:
Misfortune tames him by degrees;
For in the rat by poison bloated
His own most natural form he sees.

taberna_auerbach_0147.speaker: narrator
stanzas: FAUST AND MEPHISTOPHELES

taberna_auerbach_0148.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Before all else, I bring thee hither
Where boon companions meet together,
To let thee see how smooth life runs away.
Here, for the folk, each day’s a holiday:
With little wit, and ease to suit them,
They whirl in narrow, circling trails,
Like kittens playing with their tails?
And if no headache persecute them,
So long the host may credit give,
They merrily and careless live.

taberna_auerbach_0164.speaker: brander
stanzas: The fact is easy to unravel,
Their air’s so odd, they’ve just returned from travel:
A single hour they’ve not been here.

taberna_auerbach_0168.speaker: frosch
stanzas: You’ve verily hit the truth! Leipzig to me is dear:
Paris in miniature, how it refines its people!

taberna_auerbach_0172.speaker: siebel
stanzas: Who are the strangers, should you guess?

taberna_auerbach_0173.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Let me alone! I’ll set them first to drinking,
And then, as one a child’s tooth draws, with cleverness,
I’ll worm their secret out, I’m thinking.
They’re of a noble house, that’s very clear:
Haughty and discontented they appear.

taberna_auerbach_0180.speaker: brander
stanzas: They’re mountebanks, upon a revel.

taberna_auerbach_0182.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Perhaps.

taberna_auerbach_0183.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Look out, I’ll smoke them now!

taberna_auerbach_0186.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Not if he had them by the neck, I vow,
Would e’er these people scent the Devil!

taberna_auerbach_0190.speaker: faust
stanzas: Fair greeting, gentlemen!

taberna_auerbach_0191.speaker: siebel
stanzas: Our thanks: we give the same.

taberna_auerbach_0192.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Murmurs, inspecting MEPHISTOPHELES from the side.

taberna_auerbach_0193.speaker: siebel
stanzas: In one foot is the fellow lame?

taberna_auerbach_0194.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Is it permitted that we share your leisure?
In place of cheering drink, which one seeks vainly here,
Your company shall give us pleasure.

taberna_auerbach_0199.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: A most fastidious person you appear.

taberna_auerbach_0200.speaker: frosch
stanzas: No doubt ’twas late when you from Rippach started?
And supping there with Hans occasioned your delay?

taberna_auerbach_0203.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: We passed, without a call, to-day.
At our last interview, before we parted
Much of his cousins did he speak, entreating
That we should give to each his kindly greeting.

taberna_auerbach_0207.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He bows to FROSCH.

taberna_auerbach_0208.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: You have it now! he understands.

taberna_auerbach_0208.speaker: siebel
stanzas: A knave sharp-set!

taberna_auerbach_0209.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Just wait awhile: I’ll have him yet.

taberna_auerbach_0211.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: If I am right, we heard the sound
Of well-trained voices, singing chorus;
And truly, song must here rebound
Superbly from the arches o’er us.

taberna_auerbach_0216.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Are you, perhaps, a virtuoso?

taberna_auerbach_0217.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: O no! my wish is great, my power is only so-so.

taberna_auerbach_0220.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Give us a song!

taberna_auerbach_0221.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: If you desire, a number.

taberna_auerbach_0222.speaker: siebel
stanzas: So that it be a bran-new strain!

taberna_auerbach_0223.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: We’ve just retraced our way from. Spain,
The lovely land of wine, and song, and slumber.

taberna_auerbach_0226.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Sings.

taberna_auerbach_0227.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: There was a king once reigning,
Who had a big black flea—

taberna_auerbach_0229.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Hear, hear! A flea! D’ye rightly take the jest?
I call a flea a tidy guest.

taberna_auerbach_0232.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: There was a king once reigning,
Who had a big black flea,
And loved him past explaining,
As his own son were he.
He called his man of stitches;
The tailor came straightway:
Here, measure the lad for breeches.
And measure his coat, I say!

taberna_auerbach_0240.speaker: brander
stanzas: But mind, allow the tailor no caprices:
Enjoin upon him, as his head is dear,
To most exactly measure, sew and shear,
So that the breeches have no creases!

taberna_auerbach_0244.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: In silk and velvet gleaming
He now was wholly drest—
Had a coat with ribbons streaming,
A cross upon his breast.
He had the first of stations,
A minister’s star and name;
And also all his relations
Great lords at court became.
And the lords and ladies of honor
Were plagued, awake and in bed;
The queen she got them upon her,
The maids were bitten and bled.
And they did not dare to brush them,
Or scratch them, day or night:
We crack them and we crush them,
At once, whene’er they bite.

taberna_auerbach_0260.speaker: chorus
stanzas: We crack them and we crush them,
At once, whene’er they bite!

taberna_auerbach_0262.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Bravo! bravo! that was fine.

taberna_auerbach_0263.speaker: siebel
stanzas: Every flea may it so befall!

taberna_auerbach_0265.speaker: brander
stanzas: Point your fingers and nip them all!

taberna_auerbach_0267.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Hurrah for Freedom! Hurrah for wine!

taberna_auerbach_0269.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: I fain would drink with you, my glass to Freedom clinking,
If ’twere a better wine that here I see you drinking.

taberna_auerbach_0271.speaker: siebel
stanzas: Don’t let us hear that speech again!

taberna_auerbach_0273.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Did I not fear the landlord might complain,
I’d treat these worthy guests, with pleasure,
To some from out our cellar’s treasure.

taberna_auerbach_0275.speaker: siebel
stanzas: Just treat, and let the landlord me arraign!

taberna_auerbach_0276.speaker: frosch
stanzas: And if the wine be good, our praises shall be ample.
But do not give too very small a sample;
For, if its quality I decide,
With a good mouthful I must be supplied.

taberna_auerbach_0282.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: They’re from the Rhine! I guessed as much, before.

taberna_auerbach_0283.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Bring me a gimlet here!

taberna_auerbach_0284.speaker: brander
stanzas: What shall therewith be done?
You’ve not the casks already at the door?

taberna_auerbach_0287.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Yonder, within the landlord’s box of tools, there’s one!

taberna_auerbach_0287.speaker: narrator
stanzas: To FROSCH.

taberna_auerbach_0289.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Now, give me of your taste some intimation.

taberna_auerbach_0291.speaker: frosch
stanzas: How do you mean? Have you so many kinds?

taberna_auerbach_0292.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: The choice is free: make up your minds.

taberna_auerbach_0293.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Aha! you lick your chops, from sheer anticipation.

taberna_auerbach_0294.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Good! if I have the choice, so let the wine be Rhenish!
Our Fatherland can best the sparkling cup replenish.

taberna_auerbach_0294.speaker: narrator
stanzas: MEPHISTOPHELES (boring a hole in the edge of the table, at the place where FROSCH sits)

taberna_auerbach_0297.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Get me a little wax, to make the stoppers, quick!

taberna_auerbach_0299.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Ah! I perceive a juggler’s trick.

taberna_auerbach_0301.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: And you?

taberna_auerbach_0302.speaker: brander
stanzas: Champagne shall be my wine,
And let it sparkle fresh and fine!

taberna_auerbach_0304.speaker: narrator
stanzas: MEPHISTOPHELES (bores: in the meantime one has made the wax stoppers, and plugged the holes with them.)

taberna_auerbach_0305.speaker: brander
stanzas: What’s foreign one can’t always keep quite clear of,
For good things, oft, are not so near;
A German can’t endure the French to see or hear of,
Yet drinks their wines with hearty cheer.

taberna_auerbach_0305.speaker: narrator
stanzas: SIEBEL (as MEPHISTOPHELES approaches his seat)

taberna_auerbach_0311.speaker: siebel
stanzas: For me, I grant, sour wine is out of place;
Fill up my glass with sweetest, will you?

taberna_auerbach_0314.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Tokay shall flow at once, to fill you!

taberna_auerbach_0315.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: No—look me, Sirs, straight in the face!
I see you have your fun at our expense.

taberna_auerbach_0318.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: O no! with gentlemen of such pretence,
That were to venture far, indeed.
Speak out, and make your choice with speed!
With what a vintage can I serve you?

taberna_auerbach_0322.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: With any—only satisfy our need.

taberna_auerbach_0323.speaker: narrator
stanzas: After the holes have been bored and plugged

taberna_auerbach_0324.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Grapes the vine-stem bears,
Horns the he-goat wears!
The grapes are juicy, the vines are wood,
The wooden table gives wine as good!
Into the depths of Nature peer,—
Only believe there’s a miracle here!
Now draw the stoppers, and drink your fill!

taberna_auerbach_0338.speaker: narrator
stanzas: ALL (as they draw out the stoppers, and the wine which has been desired flows into the glass of each)

taberna_auerbach_0339.speaker: everyone
stanzas: O beautiful fountain, that flows at will!

taberna_auerbach_0341.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: But have a care that you nothing spill!

taberna_auerbach_0341.speaker: narrator
stanzas: They drink repeatedly.

taberna_auerbach_0343.speaker: everyone
stanzas: As ’twere five hundred hogs, we feel
So cannibalic jolly!

taberna_auerbach_0345.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: See, now, the race is happy—it is free!

taberna_auerbach_0347.speaker: faust
stanzas: To leave them is my inclination.

taberna_auerbach_0348.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Take notice, first! their bestiality
Will make a brilliant demonstration.

taberna_auerbach_0351.speaker: narrator
stanzas: SIEBEL (drinks carelessly: the wine spills upon the earth, and turns to flame)

taberna_auerbach_0352.speaker: siebel
stanzas: Help! Fire! Help! Hell-fire is sent!

taberna_auerbach_0352.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Be quiet, friendly element!

taberna_auerbach_0352.speaker: narrator
stanzas: To the revellers

taberna_auerbach_0354.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: A bit of purgatory ’twas for this time, merely.

taberna_auerbach_0359.speaker: siebel
stanzas: What mean you? Wait!—you’ll pay for’t dearly!
You’ll know us, to your detriment.

taberna_auerbach_0361.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Don’t try that game a second time upon us!

taberna_auerbach_0362.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: I think we’d better send him packing quietly.

taberna_auerbach_0364.speaker: siebel
stanzas: What, Sir! you dare to make so free,
And play your hocus-pocus on us!

taberna_auerbach_0366.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Be still, old wine-tub.

taberna_auerbach_0367.speaker: siebel
stanzas: Broomstick, you!
You face it out, impertinent and heady?

taberna_auerbach_0368.speaker: brander
stanzas: Just wait! a shower of blows is ready.

taberna_auerbach_0369.speaker: narrator
stanzas: ALTMAYER (draws a stopper out of the table: fire flies in his face.)

taberna_auerbach_0370.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: I burn! I burn!

taberna_auerbach_0371.speaker: siebel
stanzas: ’Tis magic! Strike—
The knave is outlawed! Cut him as you like!

taberna_auerbach_0374.speaker: narrator
stanzas: They draw their knives, and rush upon MEPHISTOPHELES.

taberna_auerbach_0375.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: False word and form of air,
Change place, and sense ensnare!
Be here—and there!

taberna_auerbach_0377.speaker: narrator
stanzas: They stand amazed and look at each other.

taberna_auerbach_0378.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Where am I? What a lovely land!

taberna_auerbach_0379.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Vines? Can I trust my eyes?

taberna_auerbach_0381.speaker: siebel
stanzas: And purple grapes at hand!

taberna_auerbach_0382.speaker: brander
stanzas: Here, over this green arbor bending,
See what a vine! what grapes depending!

taberna_auerbach_0386.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He takes SIEBEL by the nose: the others do the same reciprocally, and raise their knives.

taberna_auerbach_0387.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Loose, Error, from their eyes the band,
And how the Devil jests, be now enlightened!

taberna_auerbach_0389.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He disappears with FAUST: the revellers start and separate.

taberna_auerbach_0390.speaker: siebel
stanzas: What happened?

taberna_auerbach_0391.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: How?

taberna_auerbach_0392.speaker: frosch
stanzas: Was that your nose I tightened?

taberna_auerbach_0393.speaker: brander
stanzas: And yours that still I have in hand?

taberna_auerbach_0395.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: It was a blow that went through every limb!
Give me a chair! I sink! my senses swim.

taberna_auerbach_0398.speaker: frosch
stanzas: But what has happened, tell me now?

taberna_auerbach_0399.speaker: siebel
stanzas: Where is he? If I catch the scoundrel hiding,
He shall not leave alive, I vow.

taberna_auerbach_0404.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: I saw him with these eyes upon a wine-cask riding
Out of the cellar-door, just now.
Still in my feet the fright like lead is weighing.

taberna_auerbach_0407.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He turns towards the table.

taberna_auerbach_0408.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Why! If the fount of wine should still be playing?

taberna_auerbach_0409.speaker: siebel
stanzas: ’Twas all deceit, and lying, false design!

taberna_auerbach_0410.speaker: frosch
stanzas: And yet it seemed as I were drinking wine.

taberna_auerbach_0412.speaker: brander
stanzas: But with the grapes how was it, pray?

taberna_auerbach_0414.speaker: altmayer
stanzas: Shall one believe no miracles, just say!

cocina_bruja_0001.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Upon a low hearth stands a great caldron, under which a fire is burning. Various figures appear in the vapors which rise from the caldron. An ape sits beside it, skims it, and watches lest it boil over. The he-ape, with the young ones, sits near and warms himself. Ceiling and walls are covered with the most fantastic witch-implements.

cocina_bruja_0003.speaker: faust
stanzas: These crazy signs of witches’ craft repel me!
I shall recover, dost thou tell me,
Through this insane, chaotic play?
From an old hag shall I demand assistance?
And will her foul mess take away
Full thirty years from my existence?
Woe’s me, canst thou naught better find!
Another baffled hope must be lamented:
Has Nature, then, and has a noble mind
Not any potent balsam yet invented?

cocina_bruja_0015.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Once more, my friend, thou talkest sensibly.
There is, to make thee young, a simpler mode and apter;
But in another book ’tis writ for thee,
And is a most eccentric chapter.

cocina_bruja_0021.speaker: faust
stanzas: Yet will I know it.

cocina_bruja_0022.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Good! the method is revealed
Without or gold or magic or physician.
Betake thyself to yonder field,
There hoe and dig, as thy condition;
Restrain thyself, thy sense and will
Within a narrow sphere to flourish;
With unmixed food thy body nourish;
Live with the ox as ox, and think it not a theft
That thou manur’st the acre which thou reapest;—
That, trust me, is the best mode left,
Whereby for eighty years thy youth thou keepest!

cocina_bruja_0034.speaker: faust
stanzas: I am not used to that; I cannot stoop to try it—
To take the spade in hand, and ply it.
The narrow being suits me not at all.

cocina_bruja_0038.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Then to thine aid the witch must call.

cocina_bruja_0039.speaker: faust
stanzas: Wherefore the hag, and her alone?
Canst thou thyself not brew the potion?

cocina_bruja_0042.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: That were a charming sport, I own:
I’d build a thousand bridges meanwhile, I’ve a notion.
Not Art and Science serve, alone;
Patience must in the work be shown.
Long is the calm brain active in creation;
Time, only, strengthens the fine fermentation.
And all, belonging thereunto,
Is rare and strange, howe’er you take it:
The Devil taught the thing, ’tis true,
And yet the Devil cannot make it.

cocina_bruja_0052.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Perceiving the Animals

cocina_bruja_0053.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: See, what a delicate race they be!
That is the maid! the man is he!

cocina_bruja_0055.speaker: narrator
stanzas: To the Animals

cocina_bruja_0056.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: It seems the mistress has gone away?

cocina_bruja_0057.speaker: apes
stanzas: Carousing, to-day!
Off and about,
By the chimney out!

cocina_bruja_0060.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: What time takes she for dissipating?

cocina_bruja_0061.speaker: apes
stanzas: While we to warm our paws are waiting.

cocina_bruja_0063.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: How findest thou the tender creatures?

cocina_bruja_0065.speaker: faust
stanzas: Absurder than I ever yet did see.

cocina_bruja_0066.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Why, just such talk as this, for me,
Is that which has the most attractive features!

cocina_bruja_0068.speaker: narrator
stanzas: To the Animals

cocina_bruja_0069.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: But tell me now, ye cursed puppets,
Why do ye stir the porridge so?

cocina_bruja_0071.speaker: apes
stanzas: We’re cooking watery soup for beggars.

cocina_bruja_0072.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Then a great public you can show.

cocina_bruja_0072.speaker: narrator
stanzas: THE HE-APE (comes up and fawns on MEPHISTOPHELES)

cocina_bruja_0073.speaker: apes
stanzas: O cast thou the dice!
Make me rich in a trice,
Let me win in good season!
Things are badly controlled,
And had I but gold,
So had I my reason.

cocina_bruja_0080.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: How would the ape be sure his luck enhances.
Could he but try the lottery’s chances!

cocina_bruja_0082.speaker: narrator
stanzas: In the meantime the young apes have been playing with a large ball, which they now roll forward.

cocina_bruja_0083.speaker: apes
stanzas: The world’s the ball:
Doth rise and fall,
And roll incessant:
Like glass doth ring,
A hollow thing,—
How soon will’t spring,
And drop, quiescent?
Here bright it gleams,
Here brighter seems:
I live at present!
Dear son, I say,
Keep thou away!
Thy doom is spoken!
’Tis made of clay,
And will be broken.

cocina_bruja_0095.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: What means the sieve?

cocina_bruja_0096.speaker: apes
stanzas: Wert thou the thief,
I’d know him and shame him.

cocina_bruja_0099.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He runs to the SHE-APE, and lets her look through it.

cocina_bruja_0100.speaker: apes
stanzas: Look through the sieve!
Know’st thou the thief,
And darest not name him?

cocina_bruja_0103.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: And what’s this pot?

cocina_bruja_0104.speaker: apes
stanzas: The fool knows it not!
He knows not the pot,
He knows not the kettle!

cocina_bruja_0107.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Impertinent beast!

cocina_bruja_0110.speaker: apes
stanzas: Take the brush here, at least,
And sit down on the settle!

cocina_bruja_0114.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He invites MEPHISTOPHELES to sit down.

cocina_bruja_0115.speaker: narrator
stanzas: FAUST (who during all this time has been standing before a mirror, now approaching and now retreating from it)

cocina_bruja_0116.speaker: faust
stanzas: What do I see? What heavenly form revealed
Shows through the glass from Magic’s fair dominions!
O lend me, Love, the swiftest of thy pinions,
And bear me to her beauteous field!
Ah, if I leave this spot with fond designing,
If I attempt to venture near,
Dim, as through gathering mist, her charms appear!—
A woman’s form, in beauty shining!
Can woman, then, so lovely be?
And must I find her body, there reclining,
Of all the heavens the bright epitome?
Can Earth with such a thing be mated?

cocina_bruja_0132.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Why, surely, if a God first plagues Himself six days,
Then, self-contented, Bravo! says,
Must something clever be created.
This time, thine eyes be satiate!
I’ll yet detect thy sweetheart and ensnare her,
And blest is he, who has the lucky fate,
Some day, as bridegroom, home to bear her.

cocina_bruja_0144.speaker: narrator
stanzas: FAUST gazes continually in the mirror. MEPHISTOPHELES, stretching himself out on the settle, and playing with the brush, continues to speak.

cocina_bruja_0145.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: So sit I, like the King upon his throne:
I hold the sceptre, here,—and lack the crown alone.

cocina_bruja_0149.speaker: narrator
stanzas: THE ANIMALS (who up to this time have been making all kinds of fantastic movements together bring a crown to MEPHISTOPHELES with great noise.)

cocina_bruja_0150.speaker: apes
stanzas: O be thou so good
With sweat and with blood
The crown to belime!

cocina_bruja_0152.speaker: narrator
stanzas: They handle the crown awkwardly and break it into two pieces, with which they spring around.

cocina_bruja_0153.speaker: apes
stanzas: ’Tis done, let it be!
We speak and we see,
We hear and we rhyme!

cocina_bruja_0155.speaker: faust
stanzas: Woe’s me! I fear to lose my wits.

cocina_bruja_0157.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: My own head, now, is really nigh to sinking.

cocina_bruja_0159.speaker: apes
stanzas: If lucky our hits,
And everything fits,
’Tis thoughts, and we’re thinking!

cocina_bruja_0161.speaker: faust
stanzas: My bosom burns with that sweet vision;
Let us, with speed, away from here!

cocina_bruja_0162.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: One must, at least, make this admission—
They’re poets, genuine and sincere.

cocina_bruja_0165.speaker: narrator
stanzas: The caldron, which the SHE-APE has up to this time neglected to watch, begins to boil over: there ensues a great flame, which blazes out the chimney. The WITCH comes careering down through the flame, with terrible cries.

cocina_bruja_0166.speaker: witch
stanzas: Ow! ow! ow! ow!
The damnéd beast—the curséd sow!
To leave the kettle, and singe the Frau!
Accurséd fere!

cocina_bruja_0173.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Perceiving FAUST and MEPHISTOPHELES.

cocina_bruja_0174.speaker: witch
stanzas: What is that here?
Who are you here?
What want you thus?
Who sneaks to us?
The fire-pain
Burn bone and brain!

cocina_bruja_0181.speaker: narrator
stanzas: She plunges the skimming-ladle into the caldron, and scatters flames towards FAUST, MEPHISTOPHELES, and the Animals. The Animals whimper.

cocina_bruja_0182.speaker: narrator
stanzas: MEPHISTOPHELES (reversing the brush, which he has been holding in his hand, and striding among the jars and glasses)

cocina_bruja_0183.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: In two! in two!
There lies the brew!
There lies the glass!
The joke will pass,
As time, foul ass!
To the singing of thy crew.

cocina_bruja_0190.speaker: narrator
stanzas: As the WITCH starts back, full of wrath and horror

cocina_bruja_0191.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Ha! know’st thou me? Abomination, thou!
Know’st thou, at last, thy Lord and Master?
What hinders me from smiting now
Thee and thy monkey-sprites with fell disaster?
Hast for the scarlet coat no reverence?
Dost recognize no more the tall cock’s-feather?
Have I concealed this countenance?—
Must tell my name, old face of leather?

cocina_bruja_0203.speaker: witch
stanzas: O pardon, Sir, the rough salute!
Yet I perceive no cloven foot;
And both your ravens, where are they now?

cocina_bruja_0207.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: This time, I’ll let thee ’scape the debt;
For since we two together met,
’Tis verily full many a day now.
Culture, which smooth the whole world licks,
Also unto the Devil sticks.
The days of that old Northern phantom now are over:
Where canst thou horns and tail and claws discover?
And, as regards the foot, which I can’t spare, in truth,
’Twould only make the people shun me;
Therefore I’ve worn, like many a spindly youth,
False calves these many years upon me.

cocina_bruja_0222.speaker: witch
stanzas: Reason and sense forsake my brain,
Since I behold Squire Satan here again!

cocina_bruja_0224.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Woman, from such a name refrain!

cocina_bruja_0226.speaker: witch
stanzas: Why so? What has it done to thee?

cocina_bruja_0227.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: It’s long been written in the Book of Fable;
Yet, therefore, no whit better men we see:
The Evil One has left, the evil ones are stable.
Sir Baron call me thou, then is the matter good;
A cavalier am I, like others in my bearing.
Thou hast no doubt about my noble blood:
See, here’s the coat-of-arms that I am wearing!

cocina_bruja_0237.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He makes an indecent gesture.

cocina_bruja_0238.speaker: witch
stanzas: Ha! ha! That’s just your way, I know:
A rogue you are, and you were always so.

cocina_bruja_0240.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: My friend, take proper heed, I pray!
To manage witches, this is just the way.

cocina_bruja_0242.speaker: witch
stanzas: Wherein, Sirs, can I be of use?

cocina_bruja_0244.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Give us a goblet of the well-known juice!
But, I must beg you, of the oldest brewage;
The years a double strength produce.

cocina_bruja_0248.speaker: witch
stanzas: With all my heart! Now, here’s a bottle,
Wherefrom, sometimes, I wet my throttle,
Which, also, not the slightest, stinks;
And willingly a glass I’ll fill him.

cocina_bruja_0253.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Whispering

cocina_bruja_0254.speaker: witch
stanzas: Yet, if this man without due preparation drinks,
As well thou know’st, within an hour ’twill kill him.

cocina_bruja_0257.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: He is a friend of mine, with whom it will agree,
And he deserves thy kitchen’s best potation:
Come, draw thy circle, speak thine adjuration,
And fill thy goblet full and free!

cocina_bruja_0264.speaker: narrator
stanzas: THE WITCH (with fantastic gestures draws a circle and places mysterious articles therein; meanwhile the glasses begin to ring, the caldron to sound, and make a musical accompaniment. Finally she brings a great book, and stations in the circle the Apes, who are obliged to serve as reading-desk, and to hold the torches. She then beckons FAUST to approach.)

cocina_bruja_0265.speaker: faust
stanzas: Now, what shall come of this? the creatures antic,
The crazy stuff, the gestures frantic,—
All the repulsive cheats I view,—
Are known to me, and hated, too.

cocina_bruja_0269.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: O, nonsense! That’s a thing for laughter;
Don’t be so terribly severe!
She juggles you as doctor now, that, after,
The beverage may work the proper cheer.

cocina_bruja_0275.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He persuades FAUST to step into the circle.

cocina_bruja_0276.speaker: narrator
stanzas: THE WITCH (begins to declaim, with much emphasis, from the book)

cocina_bruja_0277.speaker: witch
stanzas: See, thus it’s done!
Make ten of one,
And two let be,
Make even three,
And rich thou ’It be.
Cast o’er the four!
From five and six
(The witch’s tricks)
Make seven and eight,
’Tis finished straight!
And nine is one,
And ten is none.
This is the witch’s once-one’s-one!

cocina_bruja_0292.speaker: faust
stanzas: She talks like one who raves in fever.

cocina_bruja_0294.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Thou’lt hear much more before we leave her.
’Tis all the same: the book I can repeat,
Such time I’ve squandered o’er the history:
A contradiction thus complete
Is always for the wise, no less than fools, a mystery.
The art is old and new, for verily
All ages have been taught the matter,—
By Three and One, and One and Three,
Error instead of Truth to scatter.
They prate and teach, and no one interferes;
All from the fellowship of fools are shrinking.
Man usually believes, if only words he hears,
That also with them goes material for thinking!

cocina_bruja_0313.speaker: witch
stanzas: The lofty skill
Of Science, still
From all men deeply hidden!
Who takes no thought,
To him ’tis brought,
’Tis given unsought, unbidden!

cocina_bruja_0320.speaker: faust
stanzas: What nonsense she declaims before us!
My head is nigh to split, I fear:
It seems to me as if I hear
A hundred thousand fools in chorus.

cocina_bruja_0324.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: O Sibyl excellent, enough of adjuration!
But hither bring us thy potation,
And quickly fill the beaker to the brim!
This drink will bring my friend no injuries:
He is a man of manifold degrees,
And many draughts are known to him.

cocina_bruja_0330.speaker: narrator
stanzas: The WITCH, with many ceremonies, pours the drink into a cup; as FAUST sets it to his lips, a light flame arises.

cocina_bruja_0331.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Down with it quickly! Drain it off!
’Twill warm thy heart with new desire:
Art with the Devil hand and glove,
And wilt thou be afraid of fire?

cocina_bruja_0335.speaker: narrator
stanzas: The WITCH breaks the circle: FAUST steps forth.

cocina_bruja_0336.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: And now, away! Thou dar’st not rest.

cocina_bruja_0337.speaker: witch
stanzas: And much good may the liquor do thee!

cocina_bruja_0338.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Thy wish be on Walpurgis Night expressed;
What boon I have, shall then be given unto thee.

cocina_bruja_0341.speaker: witch
stanzas: Here is a song, which, if you sometimes sing,
You’ll find it of peculiar operation.

cocina_bruja_0345.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Come, walk at once! A rapid occupation
Must start the needful perspiration,
And through thy frame the liquor’s potence fling.
The noble indolence I’ll teach thee then to treasure,
And soon thou’lt be aware, with keenest thrills of pleasure,
How Cupid stirs and leaps, on light and restless wing.

cocina_bruja_0355.speaker: faust
stanzas: One rapid glance within the mirror give me,
How beautiful that woman-form!

cocina_bruja_0359.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: No, no! The paragon of all, believe me,
Thou soon shalt see, alive and warm.

cocina_bruja_0363.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Aside

cocina_bruja_0364.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Thou’lt find, this drink thy blood compelling,
Each woman beautiful as Helen!

calle_1.title: STREET
calle_1.subtitle: A street in the town · Day

calle_1_0002.speaker: faust
stanzas: Fair lady, let it not offend you,
That arm and escort I would lend you!

calle_1_0004.speaker: margarita
stanzas: I’m neither lady, neither fair,
And home I can go without your care.

calle_1_0006.speaker: narrator
stanzas: She releases herself, and exit.

calle_1_0007.speaker: faust
stanzas: By Heaven, the girl is wondrous fair!
Of all I’ve seen, beyond compare;
So sweetly virtuous and pure,
And yet a little pert, be sure!
The lip so red, the cheek’s clear dawn,
I’ll not forget while the world rolls on!
How she cast down her timid eyes,
Deep in my heart imprinted lies:
How short and sharp of speech was she,
Why, ’twas a real ecstasy!

calle_1_0023.speaker: narrator
stanzas: MEPHISTOPHELES enters

calle_1_0024.speaker: faust
stanzas: Hear, of that girl I’d have possession!

calle_1_0026.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Which, then?

calle_1_0027.speaker: faust
stanzas: The one who just went by.

calle_1_0029.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: She, there? She’s coming from confession,
Of every sin absolved; for I,
Behind her chair, was listening nigh.
So innocent is she, indeed,
That to confess she had no need.
I have no power o’er souls so green.

calle_1_0036.speaker: faust
stanzas: And yet, she’s older than fourteen.

calle_1_0038.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: How now! You’re talking like Jack Rake,
Who every flower for himself would take,
And fancies there are no favors more,
Nor honors, save for him in store;
Yet always doesn’t the thing succeed.

calle_1_0046.speaker: faust
stanzas: Most Worthy Pedagogue, take heed!
Let not a word of moral law be spoken!
I claim, I tell thee, all my right;
And if that image of delight
Rest not within mine arms to-night,
At midnight is our compact broken.

calle_1_0050.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: But think, the chances of the case!
I need, at least, a fortnight’s space,
To find an opportune occasion.

calle_1_0054.speaker: faust
stanzas: Had I but seven hours for all,
I should not on the Devil call,
But win her by my own persuasion.

calle_1_0058.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: You almost like a Frenchman prate;
Yet, pray, don’t take it as annoyance!
Why, all at once, exhaust the joyance?
Your bliss is by no means so great
As if you’d use, to get control,
All sorts of tender rigmarole,
And knead and shape her to your thought,
As in Italian tales ’tis taught.

calle_1_0070.speaker: faust
stanzas: Without that, I have appetite.

calle_1_0072.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: But now, leave jesting out of sight!
I tell you, once for all, that speed
With this fair girl will not succeed;
By storm she cannot captured be;
We must make use of strategy.

calle_1_0078.speaker: faust
stanzas: Get me something the angel keeps!
Lead me thither where she sleeps!
Get me a kerchief from her breast,—
A garter that her knee has pressed!

calle_1_0086.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: That you may see how much I’d fain
Further and satisfy your pain,
We will no longer lose a minute;
I’ll find her room to-day, and take you in it.

calle_1_0091.speaker: faust
stanzas: And shall I see—possess her?

calle_1_0093.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: No!
Unto a neighbor she must go,
And meanwhile thou, alone, mayst glow
With every hope of future pleasure,
Breathing her atmosphere in fullest measure.

calle_1_0100.speaker: faust
stanzas: Can we go thither?

calle_1_0101.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: ’Tis too early yet.

calle_1_0102.speaker: faust
stanzas: A gift for her I bid thee get!

calle_1_0104.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Exit.

calle_1_0105.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Presents at once? That’s good: he’s certain to get at her!
Full many a pleasant place I know,
And treasures, buried long ago:
I must, perforce, look up the matter.

calle_1_0110.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Exit.

cuartito_0002.speaker: narrator
stanzas: MARGARET (plaiting and binding up the braids of her hair)

cuartito_0002.speaker: margarita
stanzas: I’d something give, could I but say
Who was that gentleman, to-day.
Surely a gallant man was he,
And of a noble family;
And much could I in his face behold,—
And he wouldn’t, else, have been so bold!

cuartito_0010.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Exit

cuartito_0011.speaker: narrator
stanzas: MEPHISTOPHELES FAUST

cuartito_0012.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Come in, but gently: follow me!

cuartito_0013.speaker: faust
stanzas: Leave me alone, I beg of thee!

cuartito_0015.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Not every girl keeps things so neat.

cuartito_0019.speaker: faust
stanzas: O welcome, twilight soft and sweet,
That breathes throughout this hallowed shrine!
Sweet pain of love, bind thou with fetters fleet
The heart that on the dew of hope must pine!
How all around a sense impresses
Of quiet, order, and content!
This poverty what bounty blesses!
What bliss within this narrow den is pent!

cuartito_0027.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He throws himself into a leathern arm-chair near the bed.

cuartito_0028.speaker: faust
stanzas: Receive me, thou, that in thine open arms
Departed joy and pain wert wont to gather!
How oft the children, with their ruddy charms,
Hung here, around this throne, where sat the father!
Perchance my love, amid the childish band,
Grateful for gifts the Holy Christmas gave her,
Here meekly kissed the grandsire’s withered hand.
I feel, O maid! thy very soul
Of order and content around me whisper,—
Which leads thee with its motherly control,
The cloth upon thy board bids smoothly thee unroll,
The sand beneath thy feet makes whiter, crisper.
O dearest hand, to thee ’tis given
To change this hut into a lower heaven!
And here!

cuartito_0048.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He lifts one of the bed-curtains.

cuartito_0049.speaker: faust
stanzas: What sweetest thrill is in my blood!
Here could I spend whole hours, delaying:
Here Nature shaped, as if in sportive playing,
The angel blossom from the bud.
Here lay the child, with Life’s warm essence
The tender bosom filled and fair,
And here was wrought, through holier, purer presence,
The form diviner beings wear!
And I? What drew me here with power?
How deeply am I moved, this hour!
What seek I? Why so full my heart, and sore?
Miserable Faust! I know thee now no more.
Is there a magic vapor here?
I came, with lust of instant pleasure,
And lie dissolved in dreams of love’s sweet leisure!
Are we the sport of every changeful atmosphere?
And if, this moment, came she in to me,
How would I for the fault atonement render!
How small the giant lout would be,
Prone at her feet, relaxed and tender!

cuartito_0073.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Be quick! I see her there, returning.

cuartito_0074.speaker: faust
stanzas: Go! go! I never will retreat.

cuartito_0075.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Here is a casket, not unmeet,
Which elsewhere I have just been earning.
Here, set it in the press, with haste!
I swear, ’twill turn her head, to spy it:
Some baubles I therein had placed,
That you might win another by it.
True, child is child, and play is play.

cuartito_0085.speaker: faust
stanzas: I know not, should I do it?

cuartito_0086.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Ask you, pray?
Yourself, perhaps, would keep the bubble?
Then I suggest, ’twere fair and just
To spare the lovely day your lust,
And spare to me the further trouble.
You are not miserly, I trust?
I rub my hands, in expectation tender—

cuartito_0098.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He places the casket in the press, and locks it again.

cuartito_0099.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Now quick, away!
The sweet young maiden to betray,
So that by wish and will you bend her;
And you look as though
To the lecture-hall you were forced to go,—
As if stood before you, gray and loath,
Physics and Metaphysics both!
But away!

cuartito_0112.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Exeunt.

cuartito_0113.speaker: margarita
stanzas: It is so close, so sultry, here!

cuartito_0115.speaker: narrator
stanzas: She opens the window

cuartito_0116.speaker: margarita
stanzas: And yet ’tis not so warm outside.
I feel, I know not why, such fear!—
Would mother came!—where can she bide?
My body’s chill and shuddering,—
I’m but a silly, fearsome thing!

cuartito_0127.speaker: narrator
stanzas: She begins to sing while undressing

cuartito_0128.speaker: margarita
stanzas: There was a King in Thule,
Was faithful till the grave,—
To whom his mistress, dying,
A golden goblet gave.
Naught was to him more precious;
He drained it at every bout:
His eyes with tears ran over,
As oft as he drank thereout.
When came his time of dying,
The towns in his land he told,
Naught else to his heir denying
Except the goblet of gold.
He sat at the royal banquet
With his knights of high degree,
In the lofty hall of his fathers
In the Castle by the Sea.
There stood the old carouser,
And drank the last life-glow;
And hurled the hallowed goblet
Into the tide below.
He saw it plunging and filling,
And sinking deep in the sea:
Then fell his eyelids forever,
And never more drank he!

cuartito_0158.speaker: narrator
stanzas: She opens the press in order to arrange her clothes, and perceives the casket of jewels.

cuartito_0159.speaker: margarita
stanzas: How comes that lovely casket here to me?
I locked the press, most certainly.
’Tis truly wonderful! What can within it be?
Perhaps ’twas brought by some one as a pawn,
And mother gave a loan thereon?
And here there hangs a key to fit:
I have a mind to open it.
What is that? God in Heaven! Whence came
Such things? Never beheld I aught so fair!
Rich ornaments, such as a noble dame
On highest holidays might wear!
How would the pearl-chain suit my hair?
Ah, who may all this splendor own?

cuartito_0179.speaker: narrator
stanzas: She adorns herself with the jewelry, and steps before the mirror.

cuartito_0180.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Were but the ear-rings mine, alone!
One has at once another air.
What helps one’s beauty, youthful blood?
One may possess them, well and good;
But none the more do others care.
They praise us half in pity, sure:
To gold still tends,
On gold depends
All, all! Alas, we poor!

paseo_0002.speaker: narrator
stanzas: FAUST, walking thoughtfully up and down. To him MEPHISTOPHELES.

paseo_0002.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: By all love ever rejected! By hell-fire hot and unsparing!
I wish I knew something worse, that I might use it for
swearing!

paseo_0006.speaker: faust
stanzas: What ails thee? What is’t gripes thee, elf?
A face like thine beheld I never.

paseo_0010.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: I would myself unto the Devil deliver,
If I were not a Devil myself!

paseo_0013.speaker: faust
stanzas: Thy head is out of order, sadly:
It much becomes thee to be raving madly.

paseo_0014.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Just think, the pocket of a priest should get
The trinkets left for Margaret!
The mother saw them, and, instanter,
A secret dread began to haunt her.
Keen scent has she for tainted air;
She snuffs within her book of prayer,
And smells each article, to see
If sacred or profane it be;
So here she guessed, from every gem,
That not much blessing came with them.
“My child,” she said, “ill-gotten good
Ensnares the soul, consumes the blood.
Before the Mother of God we’ll lay it;
With heavenly manna she’ll repay it!”
But Margaret thought, with sour grimace,
“A gift-horse is not out of place,
And, truly! godless cannot be
The one who brought such things to me.”
A parson came, by the mother bidden:
He saw, at once, where the game was hidden,
And viewed it with a favor stealthy.
He spake: “That is the proper view,—
Who overcometh, winneth too.
The Holy Church has a stomach healthy:
Hath eaten many a land as forfeit,
And never yet complained of surfeit:
The Church alone, beyond all question,
Has for ill-gotten goods the right digestion.”

paseo_0054.speaker: faust
stanzas: A general practice is the same,
Which Jew and King may also claim.

paseo_0056.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Then bagged the spangles, chains, and rings,
As if but toadstools were the things,
And thanked no less, and thanked no more
Than if a sack of nuts he bore,—
Promised them fullest heavenly pay,
And deeply edified were they.

paseo_0064.speaker: faust
stanzas: And Margaret?

paseo_0065.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Sits unrestful still,
And knows not what she should, or will;
Thinks on the jewels, day and night,
But more on him who gave her such delight.

paseo_0073.speaker: faust
stanzas: The darling’s sorrow gives me pain.
Get thou a set for her again!
The first was not a great display.

paseo_0077.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: O yes, the gentleman finds it all child’s-play!

paseo_0079.speaker: faust
stanzas: Fix and arrange it to my will;
And on her neighbor try thy skill!
Don’t be a Devil stiff as paste,
But get fresh jewels to her taste!

paseo_0085.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Yes, gracious Sir, in all obedience!

paseo_0086.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Exit FAUST.

paseo_0087.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Such an enamored fool in air would blow
Sun, moon, and all the starry legions,
To give his sweetheart a diverting show.

paseo_0087.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Exit.

casa_vecina_0001.speaker: marta
stanzas: God forgive my husband, yet he
Hasn’t done his duty by me!
Off in the world he went straightway,—
Left me lie in the straw where I lay.
And, truly, I did naught to fret him:
God knows I loved, and can’t forget him!

casa_vecina_0001.speaker: narrator
stanzas: She weeps.

casa_vecina_0001.speaker: marta
stanzas: Perhaps he’s even dead! Ah, woe!—
Had I a certificate to show!

casa_vecina_0011.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Dame Martha!

casa_vecina_0012.speaker: marta
stanzas: Margaret! what’s happened thee?

casa_vecina_0014.speaker: margarita
stanzas: I scarce can stand, my knees are trembling!
I find a box, the first resembling,
Within my press! Of ebony,—
And things, all splendid to behold,
And richer far than were the old.

casa_vecina_0021.speaker: marta
stanzas: You mustn’t tell it to your mother!
’Twould go to the priest, as did the other.

casa_vecina_0023.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Ah, look and see—just look and see!

casa_vecina_0024.speaker: marta
stanzas: O, what a blessed luck for thee!

casa_vecina_0026.speaker: margarita
stanzas: But, ah! in the streets I dare not bear them,
Nor in the church be seen to wear them.

casa_vecina_0029.speaker: marta
stanzas: Yet thou canst often this way wander,
And secretly the jewels don,
Walk up and down an hour, before the mirror yonder,—
We’ll have our private joy thereon.
And then a chance will come, a holiday,
When, piece by piece, can one the things abroad display,
A chain at first, then other ornament:
Thy mother will not see, and stories we’ll invent.

casa_vecina_0039.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Whoever could have brought me things so precious?
That something’s wrong, I feel suspicious.

casa_vecina_0041.speaker: narrator
stanzas: A knock

casa_vecina_0042.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Good Heaven! My mother can that have been?

casa_vecina_0043.speaker: marta
stanzas: ’Tis some strange gentleman.—Come in!

casa_vecina_0043.speaker: narrator
stanzas: MEPHISTOPHELES enters.

casa_vecina_0045.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: That I so boldly introduce me,
I beg you, ladies, to excuse me.

casa_vecina_0045.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Steps back reverently, on seeing MARGARET.

casa_vecina_0045.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: For Martha Schwerdtlein I’d inquire!

casa_vecina_0049.speaker: marta
stanzas: I’m she: what does the gentleman desire?

casa_vecina_0051.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: It is enough that you are she:
You’ve a visitor of high degree.
Pardon the freedom I have ta’en,—
Will after noon return again.

casa_vecina_0056.speaker: marta
stanzas: Of all things in the world! Just hear—
He takes thee for a lady, dear!

casa_vecina_0059.speaker: margarita
stanzas: I am a creature young and poor:
The gentleman’s too kind, I’m sure.
The jewels don’t belong to me.

casa_vecina_0063.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Ah, not alone the jewelry!
The look, the manner, both betray—
Rejoiced am I that I may stay!

casa_vecina_0067.speaker: marta
stanzas: What is your business? I would fain—

casa_vecina_0069.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: I would I had a more cheerful strain!
Take not unkindly its repeating:
Your husband’s dead, and sends a greeting.

casa_vecina_0076.speaker: marta
stanzas: Is dead? Alas, that heart so true!
My husband dead! Let me die, too!

casa_vecina_0079.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Ah, dearest dame, let not your courage fail!

casa_vecina_0081.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Hear me relate the mournful tale!

casa_vecina_0083.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Therefore I’d never love, believe me!
A loss like this to death would grieve me.

casa_vecina_0086.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Joy follows woe, woe after joy comes flying.

casa_vecina_0089.speaker: marta
stanzas: Relate his life’s sad close to me!

casa_vecina_0091.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: In Padua buried, he is lying
Beside the good Saint Antony,
Within a grave well consecrated,
For cool, eternal rest created.

casa_vecina_0095.speaker: marta
stanzas: He gave you, further, no commission?

casa_vecina_0096.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Yes, one of weight, with many sighs:
Three hundred masses buy, to save him from perdition!
My hands are empty, otherwise.

casa_vecina_0101.speaker: marta
stanzas: What! Not a pocket-piece? no jewelry?
What every journeyman within his wallet spares,
And as a token with him bears,
And rather starves or begs, than loses?

casa_vecina_0108.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Madam, it is a grief to me;
Yet, on my word, his cash was put to proper uses.
Besides, his penitence was very sore,
And he lamented his ill fortune all the more.

casa_vecina_0114.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Alack, that men are so unfortunate!
Surely for his soul’s sake full many a prayer I’ll proffer.

casa_vecina_0116.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: You well deserve a speedy marriage-offer:
You are so kind, compassionate.

casa_vecina_0119.speaker: margarita
stanzas: O, no! As yet, it would not do.

casa_vecina_0120.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: If not a husband, then a beau for you!
It is the greatest heavenly blessing,
To have a dear thing for one’s caressing.

casa_vecina_0124.speaker: margarita
stanzas: The country’s custom is not so.

casa_vecina_0126.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Custom, or not! It happens, though.

casa_vecina_0128.speaker: marta
stanzas: Continue, pray!

casa_vecina_0130.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: I stood beside his bed of dying.
’Twas something better than manure,—
Half-rotten straw: and yet, he died a Christian, sure,
And found that heavier scores to his account were lying.
He cried: “I find my conduct wholly hateful!
To leave my wife, my trade, in manner so ungrateful!
Ah, the remembrance makes me die!
Would of my wrong to her I might be shriven!”

casa_vecina_0142.speaker: marta
stanzas: The dear, good man! Long since was he forgiven.

casa_vecina_0143.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: “Yet she, God knows! was more to blame than I.”

casa_vecina_0146.speaker: marta
stanzas: He lied! What! On the brink of death he slandered?

casa_vecina_0149.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: In the last throes his senses wandered,
If I such things but half can judge.
He said: “I had no time for play, for gaping freedom:
First children, and then work for bread to feed ’em,—
For bread, in the widest sense, to drudge,
And could not even eat my share in peace and quiet!”

casa_vecina_0159.speaker: marta
stanzas: Had he all love, all faith forgotten in his riot?
My work and worry, day and night?

casa_vecina_0162.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Not so: the memory of it touched him quite.
Said he: “When I from Malta went away
My prayers for wife and little ones were zealous,
And such a luck from Heaven befell us,
We made a Turkish merchantman our prey,
That to the Soldan bore a mighty treasure.
Then I received, as was most fit,
Since bravery was paid in fullest measure,
My well-apportioned share of it.”

casa_vecina_0174.speaker: marta
stanzas: Say, how? Say, where? If buried, did he own it?

casa_vecina_0176.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Who knows, now, whither the four winds have blown it?
A fair young damsel took him in her care,
As he in Naples wandered round, unfriended;
And she much love, much faith to him did bear,
So that he felt it till his days were ended.

casa_vecina_0184.speaker: marta
stanzas: The villain! From his children thieving!
Even all the misery on him cast
Could not prevent his shameful way of living!

casa_vecina_0188.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: But see! He’s dead therefrom, at last.
Were I in your place, do not doubt me,
I’d mourn him decently a year,
And for another keep, meanwhile, my eyes about me.

casa_vecina_0192.speaker: marta
stanzas: Ah, God! another one so dear
As was my first, this world will hardly give me.
There never was a sweeter fool than mine,
Only he loved to roam and leave me,
And foreign wenches and foreign wine,
And the damned throw of dice, indeed.

casa_vecina_0198.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Well, well! That might have done, however,
If he had only been as clever,
And treated your slips with as little heed.
I swear, with this condition, too,
I would, myself, change rings with you.

casa_vecina_0203.speaker: marta
stanzas: The gentleman is pleased to jest.

casa_vecina_0205.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: I’ll cut away, betimes, from here:
She’d take the Devil at his word, I fear.

casa_vecina_0208.speaker: narrator
stanzas: To MARGARET

casa_vecina_0209.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: How fares the heart within your breast?

casa_vecina_0211.speaker: margarita
stanzas: What means the gentleman?

casa_vecina_0211.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Sweet innocent, thou art!

casa_vecina_0212.speaker: narrator
stanzas: Aloud.

casa_vecina_0212.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Ladies, farewell!

casa_vecina_0213.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Farewell!

casa_vecina_0214.speaker: marta
stanzas: A moment, ere we part!
I’d like to have a legal witness,
Where, how, and when he died, to certify his fitness.
Irregular ways I’ve always hated;
I want his death in the weekly paper stated.

casa_vecina_0222.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Yes, my good dame, a pair of witnesses
Always the truth establishes.
I have a friend of high condition,
Who’ll also add his deposition.
I’ll bring him here.

casa_vecina_0229.speaker: marta
stanzas: Good Sir, pray do!

casa_vecina_0230.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: And this young lady will be present, too?
A gallant youth! has travelled far:
Ladies with him delighted are.

casa_vecina_0234.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Before him I should blush, ashamed.

casa_vecina_0236.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Before no king that could be named!

casa_vecina_0238.speaker: marta
stanzas: Behind the house, in my garden, then,
This eve we’ll expect the gentlemen.

calle_2.title: A STREET
calle_2.subtitle: A street in the town · Day

calle_2_0002.speaker: faust
stanzas: How is it? under way? and soon complete?

calle_2_0003.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Ah, bravo! Do I find you burning?
Well, Margaret soon will still your yearning:
At Neighbor Martha’s you’ll this evening meet.
A fitter woman ne’er was made
To ply the pimp and gypsy trade!

calle_2_0010.speaker: faust
stanzas: Tis well.

calle_2_0011.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Yet something is required from us.

calle_2_0013.speaker: faust
stanzas: One service pays the other thus.

calle_2_0014.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: We’ve but to make a deposition valid
That now her husband’s limbs, outstretched and pallid,
At Padua rest, in consecrated soil.

calle_2_0019.speaker: faust
stanzas: Most wise! And first, of course, we’ll make the journey
thither?

calle_2_0020.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Sancta simplicitas! no need of such a toil;
Depose, with knowledge or without it, either!

calle_2_0023.speaker: faust
stanzas: If you’ve naught better, then, I’ll tear your pretty plan!

calle_2_0025.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Now, there you are! O holy man!
Is it the first time in your life you’re driven
To bear false witness in a case?
Of God, the world and all that in it has a place,
Of Man, and all that moves the being of his race,
Have you not terms and definitions given
With brazen forehead, daring breast?
And, if you’ll probe the thing profoundly,
Knew you so much—and you’ll confess it roundly!—
As here of Schwerdtlein’s death and place of rest?

calle_2_0039.speaker: faust
stanzas: Thou art, and thou remain’st, a sophist, liar.

calle_2_0040.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Yes, knew I not more deeply thy desire.
For wilt thou not, no lover fairer,
Poor Margaret flatter, and ensnare her,
And all thy soul’s devotion swear her?

calle_2_0046.speaker: faust
stanzas: And from my heart.

calle_2_0047.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: ’Tis very fine!
Thine endless love, thy faith assuring,
The one almighty force enduring,—
Will that, too, prompt this heart of thine?

calle_2_0053.speaker: faust
stanzas: Hold! hold! It will!—If such my flame,
And for the sense and power intense
I seek, and cannot find, a name;
Then range with all my senses through creation,
Craving the speech of inspiration,
And call this ardor, so supernal,
Endless, eternal and eternal,—
Is that a devilish lying game?

calle_2_0066.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: And yet I’m right!

calle_2_0067.speaker: faust
stanzas: Mark this, I beg of thee!
And spare my lungs henceforth: whoever
Intends to have the right, if but his
tongue be clever,
Will have it, certainly.
But come: the further talking brings
disgust,
For thou art right, especially since I
must.

jardin_0002.speaker: narrator
stanzas: MARGARET on FAUST’S arm. MARTHA and MEPHISTOPHELES walking up and down.

jardin_0002.speaker: margarita
stanzas: I feel, the gentleman allows for me,
Demeans himself, and shames me by it;
A traveller is so used to be
Kindly content with any diet.
I know too well that my poor gossip can
Ne’er entertain such an experienced man.

jardin_0010.speaker: faust
stanzas: A look from thee, a word, more entertains
Than all the lore of wisest brains.

jardin_0014.speaker: narrator
stanzas: He kisses her hand.

jardin_0015.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Don’t incommode yourself! How could you ever kiss it!
It is so ugly, rough to see!
What work I do,—how hard and steady is it!
Mother is much too close with me.

jardin_0021.speaker: narrator
stanzas: They pass.

jardin_0022.speaker: marta
stanzas: And you, Sir, travel always, do you not?

jardin_0024.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: Alas, that trade and duty us so harry!
With what a pang one leaves so many a spot,
And dares not even now and then to tarry!

jardin_0031.speaker: marta
stanzas: In young, wild years it suits your ways,
This round and round the world in freedom sweeping;
But then come on the evil days,
And so, as bachelor, into his grave a-creeping,
None ever found a thing to praise.

jardin_0039.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: I dread to see how such a fate advances.

jardin_0041.speaker: marta
stanzas: Then, worthy Sir, improve betimes your chances!

jardin_0043.speaker: narrator
stanzas: They pass.

jardin_0044.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Yes, out of sight is out of mind!
Your courtesy an easy grace is;
But you have friends in other places,
And sensibler than I, you’ll find.

jardin_0044.speaker: faust
stanzas: Trust me, dear heart! what men call sensible
Is oft mere vanity and narrowness.

jardin_0044.speaker: margarita
stanzas: How so?

jardin_0048.speaker: faust
stanzas: Ah, that simplicity and innocence ne’er know
Themselves, their holy value, and their spell!
That meekness, lowliness, the highest graces
Which Nature portions out so lovingly—

jardin_0056.speaker: margarita
stanzas: So you but think a moment’s space on me,
All times I’ll have to think on you, all places!

jardin_0060.speaker: faust
stanzas: No doubt you’re much alone?

jardin_0061.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Yes, for our household small has grown,
Yet must be cared for, you will own.
We have no maid: I do the knitting, sewing, sweeping,
The cooking, early work and late, in fact;
And mother, in her notions of housekeeping,
Is so exact!
Not that she needs so much to keep expenses down:
We, more than others, might take comfort, rather:
A nice estate was left us by my father,
A house, a little garden near the town.
But now my days have less of noise and hurry;
My brother is a soldier,
My little sister’s dead.
True, with the child a troubled life I led,
Yet I would take again, and willing, all the worry,
So very dear was she.

jardin_0085.speaker: faust
stanzas: An angel, if like thee!

jardin_0087.speaker: margarita
stanzas: I brought it up, and it was fond of me.
Father had died before it saw the light,
And mother’s case seemed hopeless quite,
So weak and miserable she lay;
And she recovered, then, so slowly, day by day.
She could not think, herself, of giving
The poor wee thing its natural living;
And so I nursed it all alone
With milk and water: ’twas my own.
Lulled in my lap with many a song,
It smiled, and tumbled, and grew strong.

jardin_0105.speaker: faust
stanzas: The purest bliss was surely then thy dower.

jardin_0107.speaker: margarita
stanzas: But surely, also, many a weary hour.
I kept the baby’s cradle near
My bed at night: if ’t even stirred, I’d guess it,
And waking, hear.
And I must nurse it, warm beside me press it,
And oft, to quiet it, my bed forsake,
And dandling back and forth the restless creature take,
Then at the wash-tub stand, at morning’s break;
And then the marketing and kitchen-tending,
Day after day, the same thing, never-ending.
One’s spirits, Sir, are thus not always good,
But then one learns to relish rest and food.

jardin_0129.speaker: narrator
stanzas: They pass.

jardin_0130.speaker: marta
stanzas: Yes, the poor women are bad off, ’tis true:
A stubborn bachelor there’s no converting.

jardin_0134.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: It but depends upon the like of you,
And I should turn to better ways than flirting.

jardin_0136.speaker: marta
stanzas: Speak plainly, Sir, have you no one detected?
Has not your heart been anywhere subjected?

jardin_0138.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: The proverb says: One’s own warm hearth
And a good wife, are gold and jewels worth.

jardin_0142.speaker: marta
stanzas: I mean, have you not felt desire, though ne’er so slightly?

jardin_0144.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: I’ve everywhere, in fact, been entertained politely.

jardin_0147.speaker: marta
stanzas: I meant to say, were you not touched in earnest, ever?

jardin_0149.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: One should allow one’s self to jest with ladies never.

jardin_0151.speaker: marta
stanzas: Ah, you don’t understand!

jardin_0153.speaker: mephisto
stanzas: I’m sorry I’m so blind:
But I am sure—that you are very kind.

jardin_0156.speaker: narrator
stanzas: They pass.

jardin_0157.speaker: faust
stanzas: And me, thou angel! didst thou recognize,
As through the garden-gate I came?

jardin_0159.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Did you not see it? I cast down my eyes.

jardin_0161.speaker: faust
stanzas: And thou forgiv’st my freedom, and the blame
To my impertinence befitting,
As the Cathedral thou wert quitting?

jardin_0165.speaker: margarita
stanzas: I was confused, the like ne’er happened me;
No one could ever speak to my discredit.
Ah, thought I, in my conduct has he read it—
Something immodest or unseemly free?
He seemed to have the sudden feeling
That with this wench ’twere very easy dealing.
I will confess, I knew not what appeal
On your behalf, here, in my bosom grew;
But I was angry with myself, to feel
That I could not be angrier with you.

jardin_0181.speaker: faust
stanzas: Sweet darling!

jardin_0182.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Wait a while!

jardin_0182.speaker: narrator
stanzas: She plucks a star-flower, and pulls off the leaves, one after the other.

jardin_0184.speaker: faust
stanzas: Shall that a nosegay be?

jardin_0185.speaker: margarita
stanzas: No, it is just in play.

jardin_0186.speaker: faust
stanzas: How?

jardin_0188.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Go! you’ll laugh at me.

jardin_0189.speaker: narrator
stanzas: She pulls off the leaves and murmurs.

jardin_0191.speaker: faust
stanzas: What murmurest thou?

jardin_0192.speaker: margarita
stanzas: He loves me—loves me not.

jardin_0193.speaker: faust
stanzas: Thou sweet, angelic soul!

jardin_0194.speaker: margarita
stanzas: Loves me—not—loves me—not—
